animation-speed.description:
Set your animation speed from 0.1 to 10, or `0` to turn animations off.
Use `2.0` for twice as fast or `0.5` for half as fast; your wallpaper uses `transition-ms` instead.

blur.description: Blur what is behind the bar, popovers, notifications and dialogs. Your compositor must support blur.

color-scheme.description: Choose `desktop` to follow your desktop mode, or `light` or `dark` to keep glimpse in one mode.

desktop-color-scheme.description:
Choose `sun` to turn your desktop dark at sunset and light at sunrise, `light` or `dark` to keep it in one mode, or `external` to let another tool decide.
Without a known location, `sun` leaves your desktop mode alone.

theme.description: Choose a theme from `~/.config/glimpse/themes` or the installed themes.

theme-variant.description: Choose an alternate look provided by your theme.

Backdrop.description:
Show a second background surface, `glimpse-backdrop`, behind your Overview in `niri`.
Add a `place-within-backdrop` layer rule matching this namespace to see it.

blur-radius.description: How much you blur your overview background, in pixels, from 0 to 128.

downscale-factor.description:
How much you shrink your overview background before blurring it, from 1 to 16. Higher values
use less memory but lose detail.

enabled.description: Show a separate background in your overview.

image.description: Source image. Unset derives it from `[wallpaper] image`.

image-dark.description: Source image under the dark color scheme. Unset derives it from `[wallpaper] image-dark`.

BackdropOutput.description:
A per-output override of `[wallpaper.backdrop]`. Every field is optional and falls back to
the corresponding value in `[wallpaper.backdrop]` when unset.

hide-unnamed.description: Hide nearby Bluetooth devices that have no name.

scan-timeout.description:
How many seconds you scan for nearby Bluetooth devices. With `0`, scanning continues until
you close the popover.

ddc.description: Control the brightness of your external monitors. Changes apply after you restart the panel.

minimum.description:
The lowest brightness percentage your display can reach, from 0 to 100. Your keyboard
backlight can still reach 0.

Calendar.description:
Share your calendar events between the clock grid, day list and `next-event`.
You get events from 31 days back to 62 days ahead; browsing the clock moves that window, with a maximum span of 400 days.
Up to 512 events are kept, with 512 occurrences per recurring event and titles cut at 120 characters.

poll-interval.description:
How often online calendars update, in seconds, unless a source sets its own interval.
Local calendars update when their files change.

sources.description: The calendars you read events from.

Clipboard.description:
Keep your copied text and PNG or JPEG images in memory until the panel restarts.
Content marked secret by a password manager is skipped; copying an existing entry moves it to the top.

capture-images.description: Keep copied images in your clipboard history alongside text.

enabled.description:
Keep a history of what you copy. Turning this off clears your history, including pinned
entries.

limit.description: How many recent clipboard entries you keep. Pinned entries don't count.

max-entry-kib.description: The largest clipboard entry you keep, in kibibytes, from 4 to 2048.

max-total-kib.description:
How much memory your clipboard history can use, in kibibytes. When it fills up, the oldest
unpinned entries are dropped.

date-format.description: A strftime pattern, e.g. `%-d` for the day of the month without padding.

FileTemplate.description: A strftime pattern naming a saved capture.

oneOf.description: Center your image without stretching it.

Geolocation.description:
Set your location for sunset times and local weather; changes apply without a restart.
Omit `[geolocation]` to use GeoClue; if you write the table, you must set `provider`.
Choose `geoclue` for the system location service, or `manual` with both coordinates; coordinates beside `geoclue` are ignored.

latitude.description: Your latitude in degrees north, from -90 to 90.

longitude.description: Your longitude in degrees east, from -180 to 180.

enabled.description: Whether the idle timers run at all.

profiles.description: Your idle actions while plugged in and while on battery.

respect-inhibitors.description:
Pause idle timers while an app keeps your screen awake, such as during a video. Each
listener can override this.

labels.description:
Your layout labels, matched by code or full name without regard to case, such as `{ "English
(US)" = "EN" }`. Other layouts show their code.

remember.description: Keep a keyboard layout for each `window`, each `app`, or everything with `global`.

on-idle.description: The shell command run when the timeout passes, e.g. `loginctl lock-session`.

on-resume.description: The shell command run on the next input after `on-idle` ran. Empty runs nothing.

timeout.description: Seconds without input before `on-idle` runs. `0` disables the listener.

background.description: Your lock screen's background image and color.

clock.description: The time and date on your lock screen.

prompt-output.description:
The monitor you enter your password on, by connector name such as `eDP-1`. Use `focused` to
follow your current monitor.

LockBackground.description: The lock stage's background: an image over a color, blurred and dimmed.

blur-radius.description: How much you blur your background, in pixels; `0` leaves it sharp.

color.description: The background color you see when an image is missing or doesn't fill your screen.

dim.description: How much the background is darkened, from 0 (untouched) to 1 (black).

dim-dark.description: Overrides `dim` under the dark color scheme.

fit.description: How your image fits the screen.

image.description:
Your lock screen's background image. If you leave both this and `image-dark` unset, it uses
your wallpaper.

image-dark.description: The background image under the dark color scheme. Falls back to `image` when unset.

Mpris.description:
Choose which media players you follow and whether to download their artwork.
Playing players take priority over paused, then stopped players, with the most recently active first.

art-max-kib.description: The largest artwork download you allow, in kibibytes, from 16 to 65536.

fetch-art.description:
Download album artwork from the internet. Artwork from local files still works when this is
off.

ignore.description:
Hide media players whose names match these case-sensitive regular expressions. Upper and lower case must match the name; start an entry with `(?i)` to
ignore case, as in `'(?i)firefox'`. Use single quotes around each entry.

hide-unnamed.description: Hide networks that don't broadcast a name.

scan-timeout.description:
How many seconds you scan for nearby networks. With `0`, scanning continues until you close
the popover.

end-time.description:
When warmer colors end with `schedule = "schedule"`, in local `HH:MM` time. Set both times
to different values; the schedule can cross midnight.

schedule.description:
When your screen uses warmer colors. Automatic mode needs your location to work out sunset
and sunrise.

start-time.description:
When warmer colors start with `schedule = "schedule"`, in local `HH:MM` time. Set both times
to different values; the schedule can cross midnight.

temperature.description:
Your screen's nighttime color temperature, from 1000 to 6500 kelvin. Lower values look
warmer; 6500 keeps the normal color.

transition-minutes.description: How many minutes the change between day and night color takes.

edge.description: The corner or edge of the monitor popups stack from.

enabled.description: Whether new notifications pop up on screen. Turned off, they still go to the history.

hide-delay.description:
Seconds a popup stays when the sending app leaves its lifetime to the shell, which most do.
Hovering a popup pauses the countdown.

keep.description:
How many read notifications you keep. Your history clears when you restart the notification
service.

max-items.description: How many popups show at once.

monitor.description:
The connector name of the monitor popups appear on, e.g. `DP-1`. Unset, or naming a
monitor that is not connected, uses the focused monitor.

suppress.description:
Block notifications whose sender, title or message matches these case-sensitive regular expressions.
Adding a pattern also deletes matching notifications from your history.

trash.description: Show your trash. Restart the panel after turning this off to remove existing entries.

listeners.description:
The actions you run after a period without input. Setting this list replaces the default
actions.

ac.description: The listeners used on AC power.

capacity-interval.description:
How often free space on removable drives is checked, in seconds. Use `0` to hide the
free-space reading.

Screenshot.description: Choose where you save screenshots and how your editor opens.

color.description: The color annotation tools start with.

cursor.description: Include the pointer in a capture.

delay.description:
How many seconds you wait before an editor capture, from 0 to 60. The `glimpse-shot capture`
command uses its own `--delay` option.

directory.description:
Where you save screenshots, with the folder created on your first save. Use a full path; `~`
doesn't expand to your home folder.

editor.description: Where an annotation opens: over the screen, or in a window.

filename.description:
The file name, as a strftime pattern expanded at the capture time. Must end in `.png` and
contain no `/`.

flash.description:
Flash your screen when the editor takes a screenshot. The `glimpse-shot capture` command
doesn't flash.

notify.description: Notify you after saving or copying a screenshot from the fullscreen editor.

stroke.description: The starting thickness of your annotation lines.

color.description: The color of the dot beside this calendar's events, such as `purple` or `#336699`.

id.description: A unique name for this calendar source.

name.description: What to call this calendar on screen. Unset falls back to `id`.

poll-interval.description:
How often this online calendar updates, in seconds, instead of using the shared
interval.

type.description:
Choose `ical` for a calendar file or online feed, or `directory` for a folder of `.ics`
files.

uri.description:
Your calendar feed URL, local file or folder. To keep a secret feed URL out of shared
config, use a `file://` path to a file containing the URL on one line.

oneOf.description:
One iCalendar document: an `https://` or `webcal://` feed, a local `.ics`, or a `file://`
holding a one-line feed URL. A local one is watched; a remote one is fetched on
`poll-interval`.

Transition.description: How one wallpaper image replaces another.

color.description:
Your wallpaper's background color, visible when an image is missing or doesn't fill the
screen.

fit.description: How your wallpaper image fits the screen.

image.description: The wallpaper image, used as-is or under the light color scheme when `image-dark` is set.

image-dark.description: The wallpaper image under the dark color scheme. Falls back to `image` when unset.

outputs.description:
Separate wallpaper settings for each monitor, matched by connector name such as `DP-1`.
Settings you leave unset use the values above.

transition-ms.description: Duration of that transition, in milliseconds.

WallpaperOutput.description:
A per-output override of the wallpaper (and backdrop) shown on one connector. Every field but
`monitor` is optional and falls back to the corresponding value in `[wallpaper]`, or
`[wallpaper.backdrop]` for the nested `backdrop` fields, when unset.

monitor.description: The connector this override applies to, e.g. `"DP-2"`.

Weather.description:
How a forecast is fetched. There are no places here: a place is registered by whatever wants to
see it, through `WatchPlace`, and held for as long as it keeps asking. Nothing is fetched and
no location is resolved until something does.

forecast-days.description: How many forecast days you get, including today, from 1 to 10.

poll-interval.description: How often the forecast updates, in seconds, with a minimum of 600.
